name: Tribes at War
summary: Mangletooth bargains for help against the Bristleback from his cage in Camp Taurajo. The captive Razormane quilboar offers intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the deaths of rival spiritual leaders.

sections.title: A Prisoner's Bargain
sections.body: Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, is held in Camp Taurajo by the tauren. The Barrens has long been contested by two powerful quilboar tribes, the Razormane and the Bristleback. The Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes. Mangletooth offers insight into who is tormenting Thork's outpost, but he asks a Horde champion to kill the Bristleback's most revered casters.

sections.title: Targeting the Earthweavers
sections.body: Mangletooth sends you north to strike at the Bristleback's spiritual heart: its Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. Killing the casters weakens Bristleback rituals, leaves the tribe vulnerable to Razormane rivals, and eases pressure on nearby trails.

sections.title: Bitter Revelations
sections.body: Mangletooth finds no peace in vengeance after the Bristleback losses. Rage replaces any celebration as he faces his own abandonment. Though he has arranged strikes to aid his tribe from behind iron bars, the Razormane have sent no rescue party to Camp Taurajo. Spurned and forgotten, Mangletooth turns to deeper quilboar secrets and the power of Agamaggan's blood.

faq.q: Why is Mangletooth locked in a cage at Camp Taurajo?
faq.answer: Mangletooth is a Razormane quilboar captured by Horde forces at Camp Taurajo. The tauren keep him caged to prevent raids and learn about quilboar incursions across the southern Barrens.

faq.q: What is the feud between the Razormane and the Bristleback?
aliases: why do quilboar fight each other
faq.answer: The Razormane and Bristleback are rival quilboar tribes fighting for territory, scarce water, and the Barrens' sacred thorn-covered grounds. Though both share a spiritual lineage tied to the Great Boar Agamaggan, they despise each other and clash over control of the plains.

faq.q: Why does Mangletooth want their spiritual leaders dead specifically?
faq.answer: Geomancers, Thornweavers, and Water Seekers sustain quilboar life, call stone and brambles into battle, and guide their warriors. Killing these casters breaks morale and weakens the tribe's fighting power.

faq.q: Who is Thork, and why does Mangletooth mention him?
faq.answer: Thork is an orc officer overseeing Horde efforts and security at the Crossroads and throughout the Barrens. His forces face relentless pressure from quilboar war bands, so intelligence on their movements is valuable.

faq.q: What happens after completing this quest?
aliases: what unlocks after tribes at war
faq.answer: Mangletooth, embittered by his tribe's failure to rescue him, offers to reveal the secret of Blood Shards. This opens the way to Blood Shards of Agamaggan, where you can trade shards found on quilboar for tribal spirit blessings.

faq.q: Where do I find the Bristleback spiritualists?
faq.answer: Bristleback Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers live in the tribe's thorny thickets, camps, and ravines in the southern Barrens, just north of Camp Taurajo.

angles.text: Camp Taurajo is ringed by hostile brush. Turning the savage quilboar tribes against each other helps protect Horde supply lines.
As a shaman, you can see how quilboar geomancers bend earth and stone through ancient pacts with spirits, a crude but potent distortion of elemental reverence.
As a tauren, you help keep Camp Taurajo secure. Mangletooth remains there only while his grudges serve the southern frontier.
